Sound Familiar?

Common Pain Management Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Fluoroscopy guidance add-on not billed alongside the injection procedure code.

PMEX bills 77003 or 77012 on every procedure where fluoroscopy or CT guidance is documented in the procedure note.

ESI billed at wrong spinal level or approach, generating payer edit failures.

PMEX selects the ESI CPT code from the procedure report, confirming the spinal level and approach before submission.

Facet injections billed for more levels than documented in the procedure report.

PMEX counts the documented levels from the procedure note and bills the correct number of facet injection units.

Drug testing submitted at incorrect HCPCS level, denied for wrong code category.

PMEX applies 80305, 80306, or 80307 per the testing methodology performed, confirmed against the lab workflow.

SCS trial or implant denied because prior authorization was not obtained before the procedure.

PMEX manages SCS prior authorization with clinical documentation of conservative treatment failure before the trial date.

Bilateral facet injections billed without modifier 50, losing the second-side payment.

PMEX applies modifier 50 to bilateral facet procedures per payer-specific bilateral billing rules.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Pain Management Billing

Pain management practices lose 16 to 28 percent of revenue to guidance add-on omissions, bilateral modifier errors, and SCS authorization failures.

PATTERN 01

Fluoroscopy Guidance Not Billed on Every Injection

Lumbar ESI performed under fluoroscopy. 62323 billed. 77003 (fluoroscopy guidance) not submitted. $65 per injection in guidance revenue not captured. At 200 monthly injections with guidance, that is $13,000 monthly in unbilled add-on revenue.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reviews every pain procedure note for documented fluoroscopy or CT guidance and submits 77003 or 77012 alongside the injection CPT code on every qualifying procedure.

PATTERN 02

Bilateral Facet Injections Billed Without Modifier 50

Bilateral L4-L5 and L5-S1 medial branch blocks performed. Bilateral modifier not applied. Payer pays for one side only. The second-side payment is lost on every bilateral facet procedure without the correct modifier.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX applies modifier 50 to bilateral facet and medial branch block procedures per payer-specific bilateral billing rules. For payers requiring LT/RT pairs instead of modifier 50, PMEX submits separate line items.

PATTERN 03

SCS Implant Denied, Conservative Treatment Not Documented

Spinal cord stimulator implant claim submitted. Commercial payer denies. Prior authorization was obtained but the authorization documentation did not include proof of failed conservative treatment (physical therapy, medication trials). Auth recinded. $28,000 implant claim denied.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX manages SCS prior authorization with a complete clinical package including documentation of failed conservative treatment, diagnostic imaging, and psychological evaluation where required. Auth documentation is confirmed before the trial procedure is scheduled.

Questions

Pain Management Billing Questions Answered

ESI CPT codes are determined by spinal level (cervical, thoracic, lumbar, caudal) and approach (interlaminar or transforaminal). We read the procedure report to confirm level and approach before selecting the code.

Yes. 77003 (fluoroscopy guidance for spine injections) and 77012 (CT guidance) are separately billable add-on codes when fluoroscopic or CT guidance is documented in the procedure note.

80305 is for direct optical observation testing. 80306 is for instrument-assisted testing. 80307 is for instrumented chemistry testing with definitive drug identification. The correct code is determined by the testing methodology.

Yes. We manage SCS prior authorization including documentation of conservative treatment failure, diagnostic criteria, and psychological clearance where required by the payer.

SCS programming visits (95970 to 95972) are billed at the correct level based on the complexity of the programming session documented in the visit note.
